newsitem.title: USA: Houston bonds flat to firmer after tax plan defeat.
newsitem.headline: Houston bonds flat to firmer after tax plan defeat.

text.p: Houston, Texas, bonds have either remained unchanged or firmed slightly since voters on Saturday defeated a plan that would have curtailed the city's tax and fee-raising ability, traders said Wednesday.
"I think they've firmed a few basis points actually," one trader said, estimating that Houston bonds improved by about three basis since the vote.

"But it's hard to tell because you also had the new deal that came into the market, which could have caused some of the cheapening to begin with," the trader said. "So you don't know how much of that differential is the referendum and how much of it is just having supply around."
On January 8, Houston sold $382 million water and sewer bonds in a negotitated offering via PaineWebber Inc. The bonds were priced at a top yield of 5.80 percent in 2027.
"It's trading I think pretty much around where it came," the trader said, adding however that the "market's been all over the place today."

The trader said the deal's 5-1/4 percent bonds of 2021 that came at a 5.75 percent yield January 8 were bid at a 5.75 Wedneday and offered at a 5.73 percent yield. The deal's 5-3/8 percent bonds of 2027 that came originally at a 5.80 were bid at a 5.77 and offered at a 5.74 percent yield.
Another trader said Saturday's vote had little impact on those bonds.
"Nothing really has impacted them at all...It didn't rebound much after the events of the weekend," he said.

The defeated proposal, Proposition A, would have required voter approval of most proposed hikes in taxes or city fees. Also defeated was a proposal to raise Houston's minimum wage to $6.50 an hour, well above the current federal minimum of $4.75 an hour.
Asked whether fear remained that the tax initiative could be resurrected, a trader said as far as the market is concerned virtually any city has the potential for such a referendum at any time.
"I don't think Houston is any different from any place else," the trader said. "But the fact that is has been defeated is (the) material matter. That's the facts."
